newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Potanin may head precious metals body.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Potanin may head precious metals body.

text.p: Russian First Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin may be tapped to lead a government commission to deal with issues on the domestic precious metals and stones market, Potanin's spokesman said on Tuesday.
Larisa Zelkova said Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin could sign an order in one or two weeks authorising the appointment.
"Potanin is for the liberalisation of the domestic precious metals and stones market," she said, but she gave no details of what he might do.

Youthful former banker Potanin, close to former reform chief Anatoly Chubais, built commercial bank Uneximbank into one of Russia's top financial institutions before quitting to assume his cabinet post in August 1996.
Uneximbank holds a 38 percent stake, or 51 percent of voting shares, in RAO Norilsky Nickel, one of the world's largest producers of nickel, platinum, palladium and related metals.
The central bank has said it is working to liberalise the domestic gold market, but its measures have yet to open up things significantly.
